title: Morphogenesis requires each cell to model its place in the target form

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Morphogenesis requires each cell to model its place in the target form

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Friston, Levin, Sengupta and Pezzulo propose that morphogenetic self-organization requires each cell to have an implicit model of its place in the final morphology, with self-assembly being cells moving to sample the local signals that model predicts (minimizing variational free energy).

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Friston K 2015, Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation › Introduction

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In this paper, we pursue the notion that morphogenetic self-organization requires each cell to have an implicit model of its place in the final morphology [21]—and that self-assembly is the process of moving to sample local signals that are predicted by that model.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Friston K, Levin M, Sengupta B, Pezzulo G, “Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation”, Journal of the Royal Society, Interface (2015), doi:10.1098/rsif.2014.1383; section “Introduction”. Scope: Cells during embryogenesis and regeneration

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-place-03: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.40

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The formal instantiation is testable, but showing that all embryogenesis and regeneration require this representation demands broad empirical data and model comparison. Existing resources can assess a restricted model rather than the biological necessity claim.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit active-inference and rival chemotaxis or regulatory-network models to spatial time series of cell position, fate, and local signals, then compare out-of-sample predictions after perturbation. Evidence that only models with cell-specific inferred target positions predict trajectories would support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The universal word 'requires' extends far beyond the toy model.

Few public morphogenesis datasets jointly measure local signals, trajectories, and fate.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.2
data existence: 0.35
analysis feasibility: 0.55
discriminating power: 0.4
operationalizability: 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The necessity claim uses an implicit model of place as the requirement for morphogenetic self-organization. Because the paper treats any adequate regulator as a model of what it regulates, a gene-regulatory or chemotactic account of the same successful patterning is counted as the model rather than as a rival. No public observation separates the two descriptions.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: A decisive test would need a fixed definition of an implicit place-model, then a morphogenetic system that reaches its target anatomy with no internal state that meets that definition. Under the paper's good-regulator reading, successful patterning itself counts as possessing the model.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Several formalizations of an implicit model count ordinary intracellular states as the model.

The necessity claim then holds for every system that already achieves a target form.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.22
operationalizability: 0.3
